title: menuz: an in-process notice posted while the first launch's alert is up has never been measured
body:
## What

menuz asks macOS for notification authorisation at its first launch (`native/macos/Menuz/Menuz/Services/Notifier.swift:18`), and on macOS 27 that first request is an alert only the user can answer. While the alert is up, a notice the app posts from its own process, through `Notifier.post` (`Notifier.swift:135`), has never been measured. So it is not known whether the centre holds it until the alert is answered, refuses it as not yet allowed, or drops it, nor whether menuz's log says which.

The app's own posts are a run that could not start (`Runner.swift:66`), a run refused because the run id store could not be read (`MenuzApp.swift:305`), and a log write failure (`AppLog.swift:31`). The placement notice waits for the grant (`MenuzApp.swift:76`). A run's notice is posted by a separate process, the wrapper's `"$MENUZ_EXEC" --notify` (`native/macos/Menuz/MenuzKit/Sources/MenuzKit/Run.swift:130`), and its not-yet-allowed and off lines under the alert were seen in ST0027's hand runs.

## Where it comes from

Point 7 of cc's review of b7e07a3 (ST0027 WP-06, 17 Oct 2026). vc's AC-06.4 hand run passed at 3e731d3 with the id already allowed, and its record ends "Unmeasured: a second in-process request while the alert is up (cc's review point 7)". `intent/wip.md` carried it as a TODO until this issue.

## How to measure

1. Book the build and the run with the node vc names for the host.
2. Build a dev Menuz.app under a fresh bundle id, outside `/private/tmp`, where macOS 27 refuses a bundle outright.
3. With hv at the machine, launch it and leave the first launch's alert up. Do not quit under it: a quit counts as no and leaves the id denied until System Settings.
4. While the alert is up, choose an item whose run cannot start, so the app posts "could not start" from its own process. Read menuz.log and usernoted's log.
5. Answer the alert, then `lsregister -u` the scratch bundle and remove its state directory.

## Fix

Decided by the run. If the notice is lost, or logged as posted when it was not, menuz logs what the centre answered, with the notice's text. If the centre holds it and posts it once allowed, the resolution records that and the code does not change.
